query: Which method can be used for oxidation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Applying stationary friction processing (SFP) to AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys reduces oxidation rates by inducing an ultrafine-grained microstructure that promotes the formation of more protective oxides.
generation.material_initial_state: as-cast equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy with coarse grains (~98 μm) and tendency to form nonprotective spinel oxides during oxidation
generation.intervention: Stationary friction processing using a WC-cylindrical tool at high rotational speeds (e.g., 1800 rpm for 5 minutes)
generation.conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at elevated temperatures (850, 950, and 1050 °C) for 100 hours
generation.structural_mediator: Ultrafine-grained microstructure with high grain boundary density (grain sizes reduced to ~0.43 μm)
generation.mechanism: The refined microstructure increases outward diffusion of Cr ions and facilitates the formation of a dense, protective Cr₂O₃ layer (alongside Al-rich inner oxides), while the increased surface free energy suppresses formation of nonprotective spinel oxides.
generation.predicted_outcome: The SFP-treated samples, especially those processed at higher rotational speeds, will exhibit significantly lower oxidation rates (lower mass gains and reduced parabolic rate constants) compared to as-cast samples, confirming enhanced oxidation resistance.
generation.baseline: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi alloy which shows higher oxidation rates and forms nonprotective spinel oxides during high-temperature exposure
generation.boundary: This hypothesis is specific to equimolar AlCoCrFeNi HEA under the studied processing conditions and oxidation temperatures; effects may vary with changes in processing parameters or alloy composition.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative improvement (exact percentage reduction in oxidation rate) and the potential influence of processing tool geometry or duration remain uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of equimolar AlCoCrFeNi HEA samples: one set in the as-cast state and another set processed by stationary friction processing at 1800 rpm for 5 minutes. Expose both sets to isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at temperatures of 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 hours. Characterize the oxide scales formed using techniques such as mass gain measurements, XRD, and microscopy.
measurements: Phase identification of oxide layers (e.g., presence of Cr₂O₃ versus spinels)
Grain size distribution of the alloy before oxidation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the SFP-treated samples do not display a statistically significant reduction in oxidation kinetics (e.g., mass gain and k_p) and do not exhibit a higher fraction of protective oxides (such as Cr₂O₃) compared to the as-cast samples, or if the oxidation resistance is not measurably improved, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does an ultrafine-grain microstructure, obtained via stationary friction processing, affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?. System: Equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Stationary friction processing (SFP) using a WC-cylindrical tool (12 mm diameter) at rotational speeds of 400 rpm and 1800 rpm for 5 min duration. Test conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 h. Findings: Grain size refined from 98 μm (as-cast) to 1 μm (SFP_400) and 0.43 μm (SFP_1800).; Phase transformation from BCC/B2 to FCC occurred, with 38% and 55% FCC fraction for SFP_400 and SFP_1800, respectively.; Surface free energy increased by 29.8% for SFP_400 and 35.2% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Oxidation kinetics decelerated by 12–20% for SFP_400 and 38–48% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Cumulative mass gain at 850 °C after 100 h was 0.33 mg/cm² (as-cast), 0.27 mg/cm² (SFP_400), and 0.17 mg/cm² (SFP_1800).; Parabolic rate constants (k_p) at 1050 °C were 23.2 × 10⁻¹³ g²·cm⁻⁴·s⁻¹ (as-cast), 18.4 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_400), and 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_1800).; Processed samples formed predominantly protective
